Thanks again for taking the call today, Maya — really appreciated the context on Catalyst's search and recommendations roadmap. Quick recap from our side and a couple items we need to validate to scope a procurement-ready quote: 

1) Monthly token volume: you mentioned spikes during indexing and daily usage from a pilot of ~200M tokens/month growing toward ~800M-1B in 6-12 months. Can you confirm the current steady state and expected peak? Any seasonality we should model?

2) Target unit economics: you said procurement is looking for a target of roughly $/1M tokens in the ballpark of $700–$1,200 depending on model tier. Is that the internal target (includes/does not include support/SLAs)?

3) Budget band and procurement thresholds: please confirm the monthly budget band that would trigger a PO vs. a contract review. For example, does a spend above $25k/month require a PO + SOW? Is there an approval threshold (e.g., >$150k requires security/compliance committee sign-off)?

Next steps I propose: I can send a simple 1-page cost estimate showing price per 1M tokens across three model bands (standard, optimized, and high-quality) and an example monthly line-item for 200M / 500M / 1B tokens. If those numbers look reasonable, we can attach a standard SOW and go to procurement.

Attaching a rough token_estimate.xlsx with the three example bands — this is just to validate ranges. If you can reply with confirmed monthly band (low / expected / high) and procurement approval thresholds, I’ll draft the formal quote.

Best,

Thanks, Jonas — great summary. Quick answers from my side after chatting with our finance and procurement leads: 

- Current steady state: ~220M tokens/month. Expected growth: 400–600M within 3–6 months as we onboard search across an additional product line. Peak (indexing runs): up to ~900M for short bursts.
- Target $/1M tokens: procurement funneling a target of $800–$1,100 per 1M tokens for production-grade models. That target should include runtime costs but excludes third-party tooling support (we handle that separately).
- Procurement thresholds: purchases < $25k/month can be done via credit card/self-serve. $25k–$150k require PO + standard MSA + our security checklist review (SOC2 evidence). Anything > $150k requires exec procurement approval and a formal SOW.

Procurement noted a 3–4 week procurement lead time for PO + MSA review if SOC2 evidence is provided; without SOC2 evidence expect an extra 2–3 weeks.

Request: Can you send the price bands with the three example token volumes (200M / 500M / 1B) and explicitly show what’s included (support, latency SLOs, data isolation options)? Also include any volume discount thresholds.

Appreciate it — Maya
Maya Singh

Thanks for the clear answers, Maya — this helps a lot. Per procurement thresholds, that maps cleanly to how we structure pricing and contracting. A few clarifying notes and an initial price band to validate: 

- What I'll send: a short price sheet showing three model bands: Standard (open models / cost-optimized), Optimized (quantized high-throughput variants), Premium (high-quality instruction-tuned models + priority capacity). Each band will show list price per 1M tokens, recommended discount tiers at monthly commit levels (50M, 200M, 500M), and example monthly totals for 200M / 500M / 1B tokens. I’ll also call out support and SLA inclusions.

- Initial indicative (list) ranges — please treat as starting points for negotiation: 
  • Standard: $950 / 1M tokens
  • Optimized: $700 / 1M tokens
  • Premium: $1,250 / 1M tokens

We typically offer discounts for multi-month or reserved capacity (Dedicated) commits. Example: 20% at a 6-month 200M/month reserve, 30%+ at larger capacity/annual commits. Those discounts can bring the Optimized band closer to your $800–$1,100 target depending on commit level.

- Compliance/SOC2: we can provide SOC2 Type II evidence and a standard security packet for procurement. If Catalyst needs on-prem/private deployment options we can include Private pricing, but that changes procurement flow and SLA.

Next step: I’ll put together the one-page price sheet + short SOW template and send over for you to share with procurement. Laura — can you confirm the recommended internal discount cadence we want to offer (early-screen: 20% at 6mo/200M, 30% at annual/500M)?

Thanks,
Jonas
